title_en: On “The Son Can Do Nothing of Himself”
author: Amphilochius of Iconium
addressee: A Christian audience, addressed directly as “you” and once as “master” (despota)
occasion: A homiletic exposition of John 5:19, defending the Son’s equality with the Father against interpretations that would make the Son a mere subordinate agent or deny his freedom.
argument: Amphilochius argues that “the Son can do nothing of himself” does not mean the Son is weak or compelled. The phrase must be read with its continuation: the Son does whatever he sees the Father doing, as one of the same nature and will. The saying was spoken to calm Jewish rage at the perceived contradiction between Jesus’ Sabbath-breaking and the Father’s will, not to subordinate the Son to the Father. Because Father and Son share one nature, will, and authority, the Son acts with the Father, not as a servant but with sovereign authority, so that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father.

outline.move: The homily opens by distinguishing two senses of “cannot” and applies them to John 5:19, then introduces the healing at the pool.
The healing of the paralytic and the Sabbath controversy lead into Jesus’ saying about the Father and the Son, which Amphilochius begins to explain against Jewish objections.
Amphilochius explains that the Son’s words were meant to calm Jewish rage, and argues that the Son cannot act apart from the Father because they share one nature and will.
The homily concludes that the Son does the same works as the Father, not by imitation or service but by shared authority, so that honoring the Son honors the Father.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The paralytic ... ill for thirty-eight years
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὀκτὼ καὶ τριάκοντα ἔτη ἔχων ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ
_unresolved_facts.fix: The paralytic was ill for thirty-eight years (ὀκτὼ καὶ τριάκοντα = 8 + 30 = 38), not thirty-eight years as stated—actually the brief says thirty-eight years, which matches. Rechecking: the brief says 'thirty-eight years' which is correct. No problem.

_unresolved_facts.claim: An interlocutor ... asks a brief question addressed to Jesus as 'master' (despota); Jesus then answers in the first person
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Εἰ οὖν οὐκ ἔχει οὕτως, δέσποτα, διὰ τί λέγεις Οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ οὐδέν, ἐὰν μή τι βλέπῃ τὸν πατέρα ποιοῦντα; Ἵνα τὴν Ἰουδαίων ὑπεκλύσω μανίαν...
_unresolved_facts.fix: The 'master' (despota) address appears to be Amphilochius addressing Jesus directly in a rhetorical question, not a separate interlocutor. The voice is the homilist's own, speaking to Jesus, with Jesus' response then given in first person. The brief should identify this as the homilist/narrator addressing Christ, not as an anonymous 'interlocutor.'

Jesus is not directly quoted speaking in u01-open. The section opens with Amphilochius' own rhetorical questions to the audience about John 5:19, and includes Gospel narrative about Jesus, but no direct speech of Jesus is quoted until u01-rem-early. The sections should be [u01-rem-early, u01-rem-mid, u01-rem-close] only.

The Greek form Ἱεροσόλυμα appears in the source, but 'Jerusalem' is not listed as a name requiring special handling in the translation brief context. However, this is minor. More importantly, the brief omits 'John' (the Gospel) as a named source.
